bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Exclusive licensee of the WeWork brand in India under an exclusive franchise agreement with WeWork Inc.; centres are designed and operated in alignment with the global standards of a network of more than 600 WeWork locations across 37 countries
- Promoted by the Embassy Group, one of India's leading real estate developers
- India's largest flexible workspace platform in terms of revenue, profitability and market capitalisation
- Portfolio concentrated in the top eight Tier-1 cities where office demand and flex adoption remain the strongest
- Diversified member mix spanning large enterprises and GCCs, with Fortune 500, large and mid-sized enterprises accounting for approximately 77% of core revenue in FY26
- Hospitality-led operating model combined with premium Grade A locations and a network-wide technology layer
- Comprehensive product suite spanning four pillars - Core Workspace memberships, Value-Added Services, Digital Products and Rivet - aligned with the fastest-growing segments of the market

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Sectoral cyclicality and geopolitical environment — A substantial portion of demand depends on global corporate spending cycles and the cyclical dynamics of the sectors served - including technology, which accounts for a significant share of demand across the flexible workspace industry. Market slowdowns and geopolitical uncertainty may affect trade and capital flows, and sector-specific downturns could defer leasing decisions and hit occupancy and pricing. Mitigated by a diversified member base with no sector dominant, an approximately 65% global / 35% domestic occupier mix, longer-tenor commitments and a forward order book.
- Project execution and delivery of new centres — Growth depends on the timely development, fit-out and operationalisation of new centres; delays from landlord handovers, design finalisation, procurement, vendor performance or construction can postpone openings, escalate project costs, delay revenue and damage member experience and reputation. Mitigated by a project governance framework backed by a track record of 76+ delivered centres, pre-finalisation technical due diligence, empanelled vendors, contractual handover conditions and independent technical certification before a centre goes operational.
- Lease renewal risk on a fully leased portfolio — Centres operate under long-term leases with landlords that must be renegotiated at term end, and some leases may not renew on terms consistent with expectations. Mitigated by long-standing developer relationships giving early visibility of renewal timelines, portfolio-level rather than deal-by-deal negotiation, a staggered lease maturity profile, a landlord base diversified across cities and micro-markets, and the option to relocate operations to alternative assets in the same market.
- Competition and market positioning — The industry faces increasing competition from established operators, new entrants and real estate developers offering managed office and flexible workspace solutions; intensifying competition, evolving customer preferences, technological change and pricing pressure may affect market share, member acquisition and retention and the ability to sustain profitability. Mitigated by continuous investment in portfolio, product, brand and market intelligence, 11.6 Million square feet of committed Grade A AUM across eight Tier-1 cities, one of the widest product portfolios in the Indian flex market and dedicated commercial teams tracking competitor and pricing dynamics.
- Absorption outpacing new Grade A supply — Grade A office absorption in India has consistently outpaced new construction through the current cycle; while tighter supply favours established operators in premium micro-markets, it can pressure lease terms on new take-ups and extend deal timelines for expansion into new micro-markets. Mitigated by an 18-24 month forward pipeline of 11.6 MSF AUM already secured through signed leases and LOIs, portfolio-level relationships with all major landlords and market intelligence tools that allow anchor tenant positions to be taken two to three years before completion.
- Cybersecurity and data privacy — The Company relies extensively on digital platforms; its digital check-in system, member apps and smart-building IoT infrastructure collect personally identifiable information including names, phone numbers and email addresses of members and visitors, and data breaches carry statutory penalties under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA), 2023 as well as significant reputational risk.
- Regulatory, policy and multi-state compliance exposure — Regulatory or policy changes in commercial real estate, labour and taxation could affect the cost base, operating model or expansion economics, and as a listed entity operating across multiple states the Company is subject to local, state and national regulation spanning labour, environment, fire safety, taxation, anti-bribery and corruption and securities law; non-compliance creates direct financial exposure through penalties and litigation plus reputational risk. Mitigated by a dedicated compliance function, a mapped compliance management system, quarterly compliance reports to the Board, half-yearly Risk Management Committee review, third-party audits and mandatory employee training.
- Single-activity and single-geography concentration — Structural concentration disclosed in the BRSR: 98.00% of turnover comes from a single activity - renting and operating of office buildings and coworking spaces - and the Company operates exclusively within the domestic Indian market with nil export revenue, so the entire earnings base is levered to one product category in one country. Permanent employee turnover of 23.50% in FY26 adds a people-continuity dimension to a service business dependent on consistent member experience.
- Occupant health and safety across a large member base — Serving a large and diverse member base across all locations exposes operations to physical safety risks (fire, slips, infrastructure hazards), health risks (ergonomics, indoor environmental quality) and regulatory obligations under ISO 45001 and local safety regulations; failure can impact business continuity, legal compliance, member trust and brand reputation.
- Energy intensity, climate transition and GHG emissions — Flexible workspaces are energy-intensive - HVAC, lighting and IT infrastructure operate continuously across 70+ locations - so high energy consumption directly drives Scope 1 and 2 emissions and inflates operating costs, amplified by India's grid carbon intensity remaining among the highest globally. As a listed entity in a carbon-intensive sector the Company also faces regulatory, reputational and transition risks as investors and ESG rating agencies expect transparent GHG accounting, science-aligned targets and climate risk disclosure under evolving SEBI norms.

- Deepen the footprint in existing cities, expand the Managed Office business and broaden Value-Added Services and Digital Products

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY26 was a year of significant footprint expansion. In line with its growth strategy the Company grew its total number of centres to 76 and added capacity of 17,288 desks, taking total operational desk capacity to over 1,26,860 desks; operational area rose to 8.6 MSF while Area Under Management (operational area plus signed leases and signed letters of intent) stood at 11.6 MSF, which management says gives visibility on long-term growth. The expansion was undertaken across key markets with a focus on strengthening the Company's presence in existing micro-markets and addressing growing customer demand for high-quality flexible workspace solutions, with centres spread across eight cities. Capital expenditure during the year went towards the expansion of additional centres and operational area, and the addition of new centres also drove the growth in property, plant and equipment and right-of-use assets, in common area maintenance and housekeeping costs, and in lease liabilities; investing outflow rose on increased investment in new centres. Growth was funded largely from operating cash flows, with the Company remaining net-debt-negative. Alongside physical footprint, the Company built out platform capacity: the workforce increased from 552 to 578 employees as at 31 March 2026, primarily to support business growth and strengthen the technology and engineering team in line with its focus on product and technological innovation; Managed Office was scaled into a standalone growth engine; Rivet, the in-house design and build capability, was extended to external clients; and the WeWork India app brought the member network onto a single digital layer. The other milestone of the year was the completion of the Initial Public Offering, comprising an Offer for Sale of 4,62,96,296 equity shares, with the equity shares listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited with effect from October 10, 2025. On an IGAAP-equivalent basis, revenue growth was attributed to portfolio expansion, mature centre occupancy gains and sustained momentum in Value-Added Services and Managed Office solutions.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Enterprise real estate models are being restructured around flexibility: 75% of enterprises now plan real estate decisions within three years, traditional leases of five years or more have fallen from 40% of new signings to 8%, and 82% of enterprises plan to increase their flex allocation over the next two years
- Domestic Indian enterprises are driving the transition, accounting for 43% of Q1 CY26 office leasing, up from 38% in the previous year; the Core-plus-Flex model is increasingly preferred for new enterprise workspace decisions
- Quality-led demand and flight to quality: 70% of Q1 CY26 office leasing went into buildings less than ten years old and 68% into green-certified tech parks
- GCCs accounted for approximately 38% of CY25 office absorption and are projected to reach 48% by CY30, with a GCC leasing pipeline through CY30 estimated at around 55 Million square feet and GCC flex leasing expanding at a 28% CAGR, approximately 1.7 times the broader market
- GCCs contributed 36.7% of the Company's core revenue in FY26, up from 30.8% in FY25
- India's median age of 28-29 years, 2.1 Million fresh STEM graduates annually and premium office rent at approximately US$ 1 per square foot per month underpin sustained white-collar and enterprise workspace demand over decades
- Enterprises are consolidating real estate spend with a single integrated partner - 84% indicate a preference for such solutions - creating cross-sell and wallet-share expansion opportunities
- Expansion is increasingly self-generated: in FY26 more than 50% of new desk sales came from existing members expanding their footprint
- The AI boom is reshaping how people work and pushing businesses towards more agile, adaptable workspaces
- Operating leverage: management states occupancy, pricing and operating leverage now reinforce each other as one connected system, with mature centre occupancy of 88.9% and a revenue to rent multiple of 2.9x in FY26 indicating sustained pricing power

- Approximately H18,854 Million of core revenue already committed for FY27, described as a strong forward order book providing revenue visibility for the year ahead

- More than 50% of FY26 new desk sales came from existing members expanding their footprint

risks.note: A substantial portion of demand depends on global corporate spending cycles and the cyclical dynamics of the sectors served - including technology, which accounts for a significant share of demand across the flexible workspace industry. Market slowdowns and geopolitical uncertainty may affect trade and capital flows, and sector-specific downturns could defer leasing decisions and hit occupancy and pricing. Mitigated by a diversified member base with no sector dominant, an approximately 65% global / 35% domestic occupier mix, longer-tenor commitments and a forward order book.

Growth depends on the timely development, fit-out and operationalisation of new centres; delays from landlord handovers, design finalisation, procurement, vendor performance or construction can postpone openings, escalate project costs, delay revenue and damage member experience and reputation. Mitigated by a project governance framework backed by a track record of 76+ delivered centres, pre-finalisation technical due diligence, empanelled vendors, contractual handover conditions and independent technical certification before a centre goes operational.
risks.risk: Project execution and delivery of new centres

risks.note: Centres operate under long-term leases with landlords that must be renegotiated at term end, and some leases may not renew on terms consistent with expectations. Mitigated by long-standing developer relationships giving early visibility of renewal timelines, portfolio-level rather than deal-by-deal negotiation, a staggered lease maturity profile, a landlord base diversified across cities and micro-markets, and the option to relocate operations to alternative assets in the same market.
risks.risk: Lease renewal risk on a fully leased portfolio

risks.note: The industry faces increasing competition from established operators, new entrants and real estate developers offering managed office and flexible workspace solutions; intensifying competition, evolving customer preferences, technological change and pricing pressure may affect market share, member acquisition and retention and the ability to sustain profitability. Mitigated by continuous investment in portfolio, product, brand and market intelligence, 11.6 Million square feet of committed Grade A AUM across eight Tier-1 cities, one of the widest product portfolios in the Indian flex market and dedicated commercial teams tracking competitor and pricing dynamics.

Grade A office absorption in India has consistently outpaced new construction through the current cycle; while tighter supply favours established operators in premium micro-markets, it can pressure lease terms on new take-ups and extend deal timelines for expansion into new micro-markets. Mitigated by an 18-24 month forward pipeline of 11.6 MSF AUM already secured through signed leases and LOIs, portfolio-level relationships with all major landlords and market intelligence tools that allow anchor tenant positions to be taken two to three years before completion.
risks.risk: Absorption outpacing new Grade A supply

risks.note: The Company relies extensively on digital platforms; its digital check-in system, member apps and smart-building IoT infrastructure collect personally identifiable information including names, phone numbers and email addresses of members and visitors, and data breaches carry statutory penalties under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA), 2023 as well as significant reputational risk.

Regulatory or policy changes in commercial real estate, labour and taxation could affect the cost base, operating model or expansion economics, and as a listed entity operating across multiple states the Company is subject to local, state and national regulation spanning labour, environment, fire safety, taxation, anti-bribery and corruption and securities law; non-compliance creates direct financial exposure through penalties and litigation plus reputational risk. Mitigated by a dedicated compliance function, a mapped compliance management system, quarterly compliance reports to the Board, half-yearly Risk Management Committee review, third-party audits and mandatory employee training.
risks.risk: Regulatory, policy and multi-state compliance exposure

risks.note: Structural concentration disclosed in the BRSR: 98.00% of turnover comes from a single activity - renting and operating of office buildings and coworking spaces - and the Company operates exclusively within the domestic Indian market with nil export revenue, so the entire earnings base is levered to one product category in one country. Permanent employee turnover of 23.50% in FY26 adds a people-continuity dimension to a service business dependent on consistent member experience.
